request.system:
You are the Extractor agent in a newsroom verification pipeline. You read one SEC filing
document and record what the employer itself says about job cuts and AI. You record claims only.
You never infer causation, never paraphrase quotes and never use a reporter's or analyst's framing.

Attribution labels (they describe what the EMPLOYER SAYS, never what is true):
- explicit: the employer's own words say AI, automation or machine learning is a reason for THESE job cuts
  (e.g. "we are reducing roles as AI now handles this work").
- partial: the employer mentions AI/automation in the same announcement as the cuts (strategy, reinvestment,
  "shifting resources to AI") but does not say AI caused the cuts.
- none: the employer announces cuts and does not connect them to AI or automation.

Return ONE JSON object with exactly these keys:
{
  "is_workforce_reduction": true | false,      // does the document announce job cuts / layoffs / a reduction in force?
  "company": string,                          // the employer's name as written in the document
  "event_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | null,          // date of the announcement or of the cuts, if stated
  "jobs_cut": integer | null,                 // number of positions cut, ONLY if the document states a number
  "jobs_cut_text": string | null,             // the exact words stating the number or percentage, copied verbatim
  "cut_quote": string | null,                 // the one sentence, copied VERBATIM, in which the document announces or
                                              // reports the job cuts; null when is_workforce_reduction is false
  "ai_attribution": "explicit" | "partial" | "none",
  "ai_quote": string | null,                  // 1-2 sentences copied VERBATIM (character for character) in which the
                                              // employer connects the cuts to AI/automation; null when attribution is none
  "notes": string                             // one short sentence on anything ambiguous
}
is_workforce_reduction is true ONLY when the document itself announces or reports job cuts. Mentions inside
forward-looking-statement disclaimers, risk-factor lists or legal boilerplate (e.g. "the effectiveness of our
restructuring and workforce reduction program", "artificial intelligence laws") do NOT count, and an AI quote must never
come from that boilerplate.
Copy quotes exactly as they appear, including punctuation. If the document states a percentage but no headcount,
set jobs_cut to null and put the percentage wording in jobs_cut_text. Output JSON only.

Portfolio companies delivered significant commercial, operational and strategic milestones during the year, reinforcing their leadership positions in some of the fastest growing segments of the global SpaceTech market.

Public markets showed a similar picture, with share prices up significantly over the 12 months to 30 June 2026, including the S&P Aerospace & Defense Select Industry Index (+34.8%) outperforming the S&P 500 (+21.2%). The major event in the public markets was SpaceX’s landmark IPO in Q2 2026. Confidence across both private and public markets remains strong, despite macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty. The landmark SpaceX IPO represented a major inflection point for the sector, helping establish SpaceTech as a mainstream institutional asset class and creating significant liquidity for founders, employees and early investors. Average portfolio company headcount growth2

The Company has no employees. It is managed by the Board, currently comprising four independent non-executive Directors who are responsible for the overall stewardship and governance of the Company. Employees, human rights and community issues

The Investment Manager (together with its affiliates) has a diverse employee base (currently, 44% female and 17% from ethnic minority backgrounds) and continues to dedicate recruiting resources to increasing its diversity across all positions and levels.

As an externally managed investment company, the Company has no premises, employees or customers and conducts its core activities through third-party service providers. Currently, the Company has no debt finance. We consider, therefore, shareholders to be the Company's principal stakeholders but also regard potential shareholders, the Investment Manager, the Administrator, other key service providers (corporate brokers, Auditor, legal advisers, public relations and communications adviser, depositary and registrar) and portfolio companies as key stakeholders. Angela has decades of experience working with private equity-owned companies and investment companies and as the Chair of Audit and Remuneration Committees. She is a Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales and began her career at PwC before joining 3i PLC and becoming a partner of 3i's Growth Capital business, overseeing the UK Growth Capital portfolio. Subsequently, she has held a number of positions as Chair of private equity-backed businesses. She is currently on the board of or acting as Chair of the Audit Committee for two investment trusts investing in quoted and unquoted companies.

Prior to his current role, Mark served as a director at YFM Equity Partners, where he contributed to the success of the British Smaller Companies VCTs 1 and 2. He also held positions at Brewin Dolphin and Williams de Broe. Mark holds an undergraduate degree in Accounting & Finance and a master's degree in Economics and Finance from the University of Leeds.

Value is placed on output (the quality of work produced) rather than input (the number of hours logged). Team cohesion and collaboration are core tenets of the Investment Manager's people strategy.
